title: Purview sensitivity labels and SharePoint ACLs
summary: Preview as of 2026-10-13: Azure AI Search can enforce Purview sensitivity labels and ingest SharePoint permissions with the content. Each carries limits on link types, guests, tenants and freshness.
useIf: Content lives in SharePoint, OneLake or Blob and access follows Microsoft 365 permissions or sensitivity labels.
avoidIf: You need GA, support for guests and Anyone links, or multi-tenant label enforcement.

explain.title: Preview, checked 2026-10-13
explain.md: Purview label enforcement and SharePoint ACL ingestion are preview features with no SLA, and the docs do not recommend previews for production [[r11]].

**SharePoint ACLs.** The indexer ingests permissions with the content. It supports inheritance, unique item ACLs, Entra groups, list items, ASPX pages and SharePoint site groups (the last three from `2026-05-01-preview`, stored with an `spg:` prefix). It does not support Anyone or People in your organization links, external or guest users, or Information Management policies, and an Entra group nested inside a SharePoint group is not expanded, so those results are filtered out. It needs application permissions, not delegated, and a Basic or higher tier [[r16]].

**Freshness.** From `2026-05-01-preview`, ACL changes on items with unique permissions are picked up on each successful indexer run through SharePoint change tokens. Changes on a parent scope (site, library, list or folder) are not: call `/resync` with `options: ["permissions"]`, or `/resetdocs` for specific keys. Earlier previews captured ACLs only at first ingestion [[r16]].

**Purview labels.** Labels are extracted from Blob, ADLS Gen2, SharePoint and OneLake and gate access by classification. They need a system-assigned managed identity, single-tenant scope and RBAC auth, and are available through REST and SDK only. In a chunked index the label must be projected to every chunk row, or the chunks are not filtered. Autocomplete and Suggest are unavailable on such indexes. Retrieval can return `sensitivityLabelInfo` per reference for banners and policy checks [[r11]]. If a label applies encryption, the user needs the EXTRACT usage right as well as VIEW before an AI app returns the content [[tr13]].

options.summary: Copy content and permissions into the index.
cons: No Anyone links, guests or Information Management policies
Parent-scope changes need an explicit resync
options.bestWhen: Sites use Entra groups and unique permissions, and revocation can wait for a resync.
options.avoidWhen: Sharing links or guests drive access.

options.name: Purview label enforcement
pros: Labels shown per reference for banners
cons: Single tenant, managed identity, REST and SDK only
Label must be on every chunk
options.bestWhen: Policy is classification-based across Blob, ADLS, SharePoint and OneLake.
options.avoidWhen: You need per-person access or multi-tenant labels.

options.name: Remote SharePoint or Retrieval API
options.summary: Let Microsoft 365 retrieve with the user's token.
cons: 200 requests per user per hour, 25 results
The caller must be known to both tenants [[r26]]
options.bestWhen: Rules are richer than an indexer can copy.
options.avoidWhen: You need your own ranking or high query volume.

explain.title: Names changed
explain.md: Microsoft Graph connectors are now Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors. They come in a synced model (content indexed into Microsoft Graph) and a federated model (MCP-based, fetched at query time with no indexing). Search for both names when you read older documents [[tr15]].

pitfalls.symptom: Chunks of a labelled document are returned to everyone
pitfalls.cause: The label was set on the parent document but not projected to each chunk row
pitfalls.fix: Project the label into every chunk, then test with a user without access

pitfalls.symptom: A folder permission change never reaches the index
pitfalls.cause: Parent-scope changes are not picked up by indexer runs
pitfalls.fix: Call /resync with options ["permissions"] on change events, plus a scheduled resync

pitfalls.symptom: Results disappear for users in a nested group
pitfalls.cause: An Entra group nested inside a SharePoint group is not expanded
pitfalls.fix: Assign the Entra group directly, or restructure the SharePoint group

pitfalls.symptom: A remote SharePoint query returns more than expected
pitfalls.cause: An invalid KQL filter is ignored and the query runs without it

scenarios.title: Sites shared with Anyone links and guests
scenarios.situation: Many SharePoint sites grant access through Anyone links and guest accounts. Security needs the assistant to respect those rules. Revocation within minutes is expected.
constraints: Anyone links and guests drive access
unknowns: Do users hold a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence?
How heavy is the query load?
scenarios.question: How do you enforce access?

options.name: SharePoint indexer ACLs and trust the result
options.why: Anyone links, guests and Information Management policies are not supported, so access would not match SharePoint.
options.tradeoff: Fine when sites use Entra groups only.

options.name: Delegate to a remote SharePoint knowledge source or the Retrieval API with the user's token
options.why: SharePoint applies its own rules live, and nothing is copied [[r26]].
options.tradeoff: Quotas (200 requests per user per hour), licensing and less ranking control.

options.name: Index only sites that use Entra groups and exclude link-shared ones
options.tradeoff: Link-shared content is out of scope for the assistant.

flips.then: The indexer with ACLs becomes viable.

flips.if: Query volume exceeds the per-user quota
flips.then: Combine indexed content for most sites with delegation for link-shared ones.

scenarios.takeaway: When sharing links decide access, let the source decide.

scenarios.title: Classification-driven policy over a chunked index
scenarios.situation: A single-tenant company labels documents Public, General and Confidential in Purview. Content is in Blob, OneLake and SharePoint. The assistant chunks documents. The team wants one rule instead of per-document ACLs.
unknowns: Is the service using a system-assigned managed identity?
scenarios.question: How do you enforce the label policy?

options.name: Purview label enforcement, with the label projected into every chunk row
options.why: It matches a classification policy, and per-chunk labels make the filter effective [[r11]].
options.tradeoff: Preview, managed identity and REST or SDK only, with no Autocomplete or Suggest.

options.name: Label on the parent document only
options.why: Chunks are not filtered without their own label.
options.tradeoff: Works only when the index holds whole documents.

options.name: Copy labels into a security filter field yourself
options.tradeoff: You maintain the mapping and drift between labels and index.

flips.then: Use the security filter copy of labels.
Users also need the EXTRACT right for AI apps to return content.

scenarios.title: Folder permissions change at the parent
scenarios.situation: Access is managed at library and folder level. When an owner changes a folder's permissions, the index must reflect it within 15 minutes. The indexer runs every 5 minutes.
unknowns: Can change events trigger a job?
How many documents sit under one folder?
scenarios.question: How do you meet the target?

options.name: Rely on the 5-minute indexer runs
options.why: Runs pick up unique-permission item changes, not parent-scope changes [[r16]].
options.tradeoff: Enough only for items with unique permissions.

options.name: Trigger /resync with options permissions from change events, plus a scheduled resync
options.why: It covers parent-scope changes explicitly and the schedule catches missed events.
options.tradeoff: You build the trigger and watch the resync load.

options.name: Nightly full resync
options.tradeoff: Up to a day of lag, so it misses 15 minutes.

flips.if: The target relaxes to a day

flips.then: Add a live check on those hits.

scenarios.takeaway: Parent-scope changes need an explicit resync.

quiz.q: Which are NOT supported by the SharePoint indexer's ACL ingestion? Choose all that apply.
quiz.explain: Anyone links, People in your organization links, guests and Information Management policies are not supported. Entra groups and inheritance are supported.

quiz.q: A document is labelled Confidential and users without access still receive its text from a chunked index. What is the most likely cause?
options: The label is on the parent record but was not projected to each chunk row
The index is on the Basic tier
quiz.explain: In a chunked index each chunk row needs the label or it is not filtered. A user-assigned identity prevents label ingestion altogether rather than leaking chunks, and tier or Autocomplete do not govern filtering.

flashcards.front: What does the SharePoint indexer's ACL support exclude?
flashcards.back: Anyone and People in your organization links, external or guest users and Information Management policies. Entra groups nested in SharePoint groups are not expanded.

flashcards.front: How do parent-scope SharePoint permission changes reach the index?
flashcards.back: Not through indexer runs. Call /resync with options ["permissions"], or /resetdocs for specific keys.

flashcards.front: What must you do for Purview labels on chunked indexes?
flashcards.back: Project the label onto every chunk row, or chunks are not filtered. Labels also need a system-assigned managed identity and a single tenant.
